title: Hideki Kamiya expresses interest in making Castlevania
excerpt:
Hideki Kamiya wants to develop a Castlevania game for Konami.
He is currently working on the Okami sequel.
body_md:
Japanese game director Hideki Kamiya has expressed interest in developing a new Castlevania game during a discussion on his personal YouTube channel. The creator associated with Devil May Cry, Okami and Bayonetta mentioned Konami while considering potential future collaborations for his independent development studio.

Kamiya established Clovers in 2023. He explained that the studio does not have outside funding and that maintaining constructive relationships with established publishers is important if the team wants to continue developing projects that interest its members. Capcom, Nintendo, PlayStation and Konami were among the companies mentioned during the discussion.

When the conversation turned to Konami, Kamiya brought up both Castlevania and Getsu Fuma Den. He expressed confidence that his team could create an impressive Castlevania installment if given the opportunity, while acknowledging that he is currently occupied with another project.

That project is the sequel to Okami, which was announced in 2024. Kamiya also discussed possible collaborations involving other established properties, including Star Fox and King's Knight. These ideas were presented as personal ambitions rather than announcements of projects that have entered production.

His enthusiasm for Castlevania is longstanding. In a 2025 interview with Famitsu, Kamiya identified the franchise as one of the games that had influenced him. In an earlier interview in 2006, he praised the original Castlevania for its coherent design and the sense of purpose evident in its environments and progression.

He particularly appreciated the way the castle's architecture and the player's journey through its different areas communicated a story without relying on unnecessary elements. Those observations provide context for his interest in the franchise beyond the commercial appeal of working with a recognizable property.

Konami has increasingly collaborated with external development teams on established franchises in recent years. Several Silent Hill projects have involved outside studios, while Castlevania has appeared in collaborations with other games. Evil Empire has also worked on Castlevania-related content, illustrating that external development partnerships are not unprecedented for the series.

Kamiya's background in action game design makes the idea of such a collaboration an interesting prospect for fans. However, neither Konami nor Clovers has announced an agreement to develop a new Castlevania game together in the available report. His comments should therefore be understood as an expression of creative interest and a possible future opportunity, rather than confirmation that another installment is currently in development.
